headline: Cisco rushed out a fix for a Secure Email Gateway zero-day that hands unauthenticated attackers root on the appliance, while Chinese operators chained patched Chrome and Windows bugs to plant the GRIMWEDGE backdoor inside non-governmental organizations.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers keep landing on the appliances that guard the perimeter, and the Cisco Secure Email Gateway zero-day gives an unauthenticated stranger root on the box that inspects every message an organization receives.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Cisco Secure Email Gateway Zero-Day Hands Attackers Root

emerging_trends.text: Criminals increasingly borrow reputation they never earned: the hijacked HBO Max account on Reddit carried ClickFix ads for 48 hours to macOS and Windows users who trusted the verification badge above them.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Hijacked HBO Max Reddit Account Spreads ClickFix Malware

emerging_trends.text: Model builders are writing down in public what their systems may do under cyberattack pressure, and Microsoft's Humanist AI Code of Conduct puts a six-week comment clock on the line between defensive research and operational attack capability.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Microsoft Drafts a Humanist AI Code of Conduct

topics.title: Cisco Secure Email Gateway Zero-Day Hands Attackers Root
topics.latest_developments: Cisco released the patch and confirmed active exploitation on September 15, 2026, detailing CVE-2026-76461 as a 9.8-rated failure to validate email parsing in AsyncOS that lets an unauthenticated remote attacker run arbitrary commands as root, a sharper account than the SQL injection entry CISA posted to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog a day earlier.
topics.summary: Cisco Secure Email Gateway appliances handle inbound mail for large enterprises, and a crafted message reaches the underlying operating system with full privileges. Administrators should install the AsyncOS fix immediately and audit the appliances for unfamiliar accounts and outbound connections.

sources.title: Cisco patches Secure Email Gateway zero-day exploited in attacks
Cisco Secure Email Gateway Flaw Exploited in the Wild, Enables Root Command Execution
Root RCE Zero-Day in Cisco Secure Email Gateway Under Active Exploitation
CISA Adds One Known Exploited Vulnerability to Catalog

topics.title: Hijacked HBO Max Reddit Account Spreads ClickFix Malware
topics.latest_developments: Attackers seized u/hbomax, the verified official Reddit account of HBO Max, and spent 48 hours running paid ads from it that sent macOS and Windows users to a ClickFix page, which talked them into pasting commands that installed information-stealing malware.
topics.summary: ClickFix cons a victim into running the attacker's command on their own machine, and the stolen advertising status of a verified brand account supplies the trust the trick needs. Reddit users should treat any ad that asks them to run a terminal or Run-box command as an attack regardless of who posted it.

sources.title: Hackers hijack HBO Max Reddit account to push malware in ClickFix ads
Attackers hijack HBO Max's Reddit account for 48-hour malvertising blitz
Hacked HBO Max Reddit Account Used for Malware Delivery via ClickFix Attack

topics.title: Black Axe Leaders Extradited to the United States
topics.latest_developments: Five alleged leaders of the Black Axe syndicate arrived in the United States from South Africa to face wire fraud and money laundering charges, and prosecutors unsealed a 2021 indictment accusing the men of romance scams that took thousands of dollars each from more than 100 people; separately, Kenneth Carter, 44, of Portland, Oregon, drew 16 months in federal prison for feeding a SIM-swap gang customer information from the AT&T retail store where he worked, part of an attempt to steal more than half a million dollars.
topics.summary: Black Axe is a Nigerian organized crime network that runs cyber-enabled financial fraud worldwide, and the Carter case shows how a single retail employee opens the telephone accounts that protect bank logins. Companies should treat carrier account access as a privileged system and monitor it accordingly.

sources.title: Suspected Black Axe gang leaders face cybercrime charges in the US
Members of 'Black Axe' cybercriminal group extradited from South Africa
Former AT&T store worker jailed after moonlighting as a SIM-swap gang's inside man

topics.title: Microsoft Drafts a Humanist AI Code of Conduct
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft AI published the first draft of its Humanist AI Code of Conduct on September 15, 2026, opening a six-week public consultation on a document that fixes a boundary between defensive cyber research and operational attack capability, sets a chain of command for its models, and lists safety constraints, with a revised version due later this year to govern model development from 2027 onward.
topics.summary: The code is Microsoft's training manual for how it builds models and how it expects them to behave once customers deploy them, arriving a day after Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei asked the industry to slow frontier improvement. Enterprises evaluating Microsoft models should read the draft as the vendor's statement of what its systems will refuse.

sources.title: Microsoft sets security and safety rules for its AI models
Microsoft AI Code of Conduct Sets Cyberattack Boundaries, Chain of Command, Safety Constraints

topics.title: UTA0560 Plants GRIMWEDGE in NGOs
topics.latest_developments: Volexity reported on September 15, 2026 that the Chinese threat cluster it tracks as UTA0560 spear-phished several non-governmental organizations on September 1, 2026, chaining recently patched Google Chrome and Microsoft Windows flaws to drop a JavaScript backdoor the firm named GRIMWEDGE.
topics.summary: GRIMWEDGE arrives through a browser exploit chain that fires on a single spear-phishing click and leaves a JavaScript implant behind, the fourth Chrome and Windows chain researchers have documented this month. Organizations running Chrome should confirm they have the September updates on every endpoint.

sources.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploit Chrome-Windows Zero-Day Chain to Deploy GRIMWEDGE

topics.title: Japan's Digital Agency VPN Flaw Exposes 246,000 Records
topics.latest_developments: Japan's Digital Agency disclosed a breach that may have exposed roughly 246,000 record rows of personal information on government employees, which intruders reached through a flaw in the agency's VPN.
topics.summary: The Digital Agency runs the Japanese government's shared digital infrastructure, so the exposed rows cover staff across ministries. Agencies relying on the same VPN products should assume credential reuse and force resets.

sources.title: Japan's Digital Agency says VPN flaw exposed 246,000 personnel records

business_politics.title: Ten-Year Treasury Yield Tops 5%
business_politics.latest_developments: The 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.04% Tuesday morning, September 15, the highest since 2007, and 10-year German and Japanese government yields hit multiyear highs as U.S. stock futures slid a day before the Federal Reserve decides on rates.
business_politics.summary: A global bond selloff has lifted long-term borrowing costs past levels last seen before the financial crisis, with traders pricing a Federal Reserve increase Wednesday, September 16, on the strength of Brent crude near $108 a barrel and record American diesel prices. The Wall Street Journal reported the same morning that regulators have begun scrutinizing the growing Treasury market footprint of hedge funds, a concentration that amplifies any dislocation.

sources.title: Global Bond Selloff Deepens as 10-Year Yields Hit Multiyear Highs
Ten-year Treasury yield hits highest since global financial crisis
Stock Futures Retreat, 10-Year Treasury Yield Holds Above 5% as Investors Await Fed Decision
Hedge Funds Face Scrutiny Over Growing Treasury Footprint

business_politics.title: Supreme Court Blocks Trump's Mail Ballot Rules
business_politics.latest_developments: The U.S. Supreme Court rejected the Trump administration's new mail-ballot requirements Monday night, September 14, in an unsigned order from which Justices Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas dissented.
business_politics.summary: President Trump's executive order would have imposed fresh requirements on mail voting weeks before the November congressional elections, with voting already underway in some states; a federal appeals court blocked it September 10 and the administration sought emergency relief. Election administrators had warned that implementing new rules this late would throw the midterms into a scramble.

sources.title: Supreme Court rejects Trump's mail-in ballot restrictions for midterms
The Supreme Court blocked the Trump administration from imposing new requirements for mail ballots, averting what officials warned would have been a crisis in the midterm elections

business_politics.title: Diesel Sets a Record at $6.27
business_politics.latest_developments: The average U.S. diesel price hit a record $6.27 a gallon Tuesday, September 15, hardening expectations of a Federal Reserve rate increase, while Brent traded at $107.59 with Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline still shut.
business_politics.summary: Drones fired from Iraq knocked out the line that moves Saudi crude from the eastern oil fields to the Red Sea, and Houthi forces have seized territory commanding the Bab al-Mandeb corridor, leaving Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman fighting on two fronts. American manufacturers report a fresh burst of supply chain cost inflation from the Iran war, tariffs, and AI-driven component scarcity.

sources.title: U.S. Diesel Prices Hit New Record High as Fuel Squeeze Bites
Oil Prices Rise as Middle East Supply Concerns Persist
War 'on all fronts' tests Saudi Arabia's crown prince
US manufacturers hit by fresh burst of supply chain cost inflation

business.title: Liquor Money as Growth Money
business.latest_developments: Post-Gazette columnist Brandon McGinley argued Tuesday, September 15, that Pennsylvania should study how Ohio turns state liquor sales profits into economic development through JobsOhio.
business.summary: Ohio pledges the profits of its state liquor enterprise to JobsOhio, the private nonprofit that recruits employers and readies industrial sites, giving the state a dedicated stream of deal money. Pennsylvania runs its own liquor stores through the Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board and pays for site preparation out of Governor Josh Shapiro's PA SITES program, which competes for general fund dollars every budget cycle.

sources.title: Brandon McGinley: How Ohio juices growth with liquor sales, and what we can learn from it

business.title: KLVN Closes and the Gobblerito Turns 20
business.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper reported Tuesday, September 15, that KLVN Coffee Lab has closed and that Mad Mex's Gobblerito reaches its 20th year, alongside fresh word on Penn Brewery, Acrisure Stadium concessions, and Jackworth Ginger Beer.
business.summary: KLVN Coffee Lab shuts its doors as the Gobblerito, the Thanksgiving-dinner burrito that Mad Mex sells each fall, marks two decades on the menu. Penn Brewery, the Troy Hill brewer that filed for bankruptcy five months ago, has landed new owners.

sources.title: The Gobblerito turns 20, KLVN closes, and more Pittsburgh food news
Pittsburgh's oldest brewery receives new owners

business.title: Riverfront Theater Moves Downtown
business.latest_developments: TribLive reported Tuesday, September 15, that Riverfront Theater Company has left Aspinwall for a space in Pittsburgh's Cultural District, keeping its name.
business.summary: Riverfront Theater Company built its audience in the Allegheny River borough of Aspinwall and now joins the concentration of stages in the Cultural District downtown. The move puts a small producing company inside the same blocks as the Benedum Center and the Byham Theater.

sources.title: Riverfront Theater Company relocates from Aspinwall to Pittsburgh's Cultural District

around_town.title: Pitcairn Council Keeps Its ICE Agreement
around_town.latest_developments: Pitcairn Borough Council voted 5-2 on Monday, September 14, against a resolution to terminate the borough police department's cooperation agreement with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.
around_town.summary: Pitcairn entered the 287(g) agreement, which deputizes local officers to perform federal immigration functions, without public input or a council vote, and residents filled a heated meeting to demand that the council undo it. The vote runs opposite the direction taken in Stowe Township, where commissioners rescinded their own 287(g) agreement earlier this month.

sources.title: Pitcairn council votes down resolution to end police ICE agreement
Pitcairn council declines to rescind police partnership with ICE
Pitcairn's agreement with ICE the topic of debate at council meeting
Pitcairn council meeting erupts over police agreement with ICE

around_town.title: 1,400 Comments on Paid Parental Leave
around_town.latest_developments: PublicSource reported Tuesday, September 15, that Allegheny County collected about 1,400 public comments on its paid parental leave proposal, a record for the county, and that the tally shows broad support, a deep split, and appetite for changes to the bill.
around_town.summary: The legislation before Allegheny County Council would give county employees 18 weeks of paid parental leave, a signature item for County Executive Sara Innamorato as she seeks reelection, and the Council's health committee held a public hearing on it September 10. Residents now get another window to weigh in on possible amendments.

sources.title: 1,400 paid parental leave comments show support, deep split, room for change

around_town.title: Plum Backs Clover Commons Residents
around_town.latest_developments: Plum Borough Council passed a resolution urging the Pennsylvania legislature to act for residents of Clover Commons facing steep land rent increases, and TribLive's editorial board pressed the state Senate the same day, September 15, to move on manufactured home protections.
around_town.summary: Nearly 60 residents of Clover Commons, a senior manufactured home community in Plum, marched through their own streets last week over land rent that has climbed by roughly a third in a few years, and asked state senators to pass House Bill 1250. Homeowners in such communities own the house and rent the ground beneath it, which leaves them exposed when an owner raises the rent.

sources.title: Plum Borough Council backing Clover Commons residents as they face rent increases
Editorial: Senate should move on manufactured home protections

events.title: Flight 93 Chalk Portraits in Somerset
events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Tuesday, September 15, that the chalk portraits of the 40 Flight 93 passengers and crew will stay on view in Somerset through Sunday, September 20.
events.summary: Artists drew the portraits in chalk for the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001, attacks, and organizers are preserving them in Somerset, the Somerset County seat about 15 miles from the Flight 93 National Memorial in Stonycreek Township. Visitors can see them through Sunday, September 20.

sources.title: Chalk portraits of Flight 93 crew and passengers will be preserved until Sunday in Somerset

events.title: Film on Film at Row House Hollywood
events.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper profiled projectionist Katerina Sarandou on Tuesday, September 15, who has run the booth at Row House Hollywood since the theater's first screening.
events.summary: Row House Hollywood programs 35mm and 70mm prints for audiences that want movies projected the pre-digital way, and Sarandou threads and runs every one of them. The theater is the second house from the Row House team, which started with Row House Cinema in Lawrenceville.

sources.title: Katerina Sarandou revives the art of film projection at Row House Hollywood

around_teams.title: SNR Drive Turns the Page to New England
around_teams.latest_developments: Matt Williamson and Wes Uhler spent Monday's SNR Drive, posted September 14 on the Steelers' channel, reviewing the Week 1 win over the Atlanta Falcons and head coach Mike McCarthy's Monday news conference, and the club began promoting Week 2 at the New England Patriots, Sunday, September 20, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS.
around_teams.summary: SNR Drive is the Steelers' daily radio and video show, and Williamson, a former NFL scout, works through the tape and the coach's remarks with Uhler each weekday. McCarthy, in his first season running the team, met reporters Monday to open preparation for the trip to Foxborough.

sources.title: Recapping Yesterday's 20-13 Win Against The Falcons | SNR Drive (Sept.14) | Pittsburgh Steelers
Coach McCarthy Press Conference (Week 2 at New England Patriots) | Pittsburgh Steelers

team_usa.title: Colombia Courts Alexander Shaw
team_usa.latest_developments: A source told ESPN on Tuesday, September 15, that Colombia has contacted Inter Miami midfielder Alexander Shaw, who played for the United States under-20 team in this year's Concacaf tournament, setting up a fight over his international future.
team_usa.summary: Shaw holds dual nationality, and a player who has appeared only in youth competition may still switch federations before committing at the senior level. The United States developed him through its under-20 program, and Colombia now aims to pull him the other way.

sources.title: Source: Colombia targeting U.S. U20 dual national Alexander Shaw

reading.title: OpenAI Ads, Amazon Ads in ChatGPT, Walmart to Accept Apple Pay
reading.summary: Ben Thompson argues that advertising inside ChatGPT is already working and that it hands Amazon an answer to the problem chatbots pose to its retail search business. He reads Walmart's decision to accept Apple Pay as proof that fighting an entrenched standard costs more than joining it.

reading.author: Ed Zitron
reading.title: AI Is Already In Dangerous Hands
reading.summary: Zitron contends that the speculative case about future superintelligence distracts from the concrete harm the people running today's AI companies are doing with the technology they already control.

reading.author: Cal Newport
reading.title: Superintelligence is a Fairy Tale. But Chasing It Can Still Cause Harm.
reading.summary: Newport dismisses the prospect of self-improving superintelligence as a story the industry tells itself, writing in response to Anthropic employees who said publicly that their work could kill billions. He argues the pursuit still does damage through the money, energy, and social disruption it consumes along the way.
